newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: U.N.'s Annan offers monitors for Zaire ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: U.N.'s Annan offers monitors for Zaire ceasefire.

text.p: United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Thursday the U.N. Security Council would consider a peace monitoring force for Zaire if the warring sides agreed to a ceasefire.

Annan said after talks with South African President Nelson Mandela he was hopeful that a proposed summit in Lome, Togo, on March 26 would bring the government and Laurent Kabila's rebels closer together.
"If a ceasefire is agreed to, the Council will have to consider the possibility of establishing a monitoring mechanism and that can only be done by troops," he said.
Annan said both sides had indicated in preliminary talks with mediators that they would look to the United Nations for help to monitor a ceasefire.
"It is not excluded, if there were to be a ceasefire agreement signed by the parties and if it were to hold, that the U.N. would put in peacekeepers to monitor it," he said.
Annan said he was hopeful that the Lome summit would lead to peace.
"What is important to note is that no one, not even the rebel leaders, has pressed for secession or the breakup of Zaire.
"What they say they are seeking is change in leadership. That change in leadership can be attained in many other ways, including through the ballot box," he said.
